Fovector is the macro alias for `F->ovector`, and `heapframe` declares `PCRE2_SIZE ovector[2]` as its final field. The immediately following vulnerable lines save and restore `Fovector[-2]` and `Fovector[-1]`, so this code is explicitly treating the two preceding `PCRE2_SIZE` slots as synthetic overall-match offsets for callouts. The fixing commit introduces a separate `callout_ovector` pointer and replaces the direct negative-index form on `Fovector`.

The one-byte PoC 0x26 ('&') is both the entire pattern and the seed byte at data[size/2]. The harness deterministically derives the initial compile_options from that byte; because the saved crash later reaches do_callout even though '&' has no explicit callout syntax, the crashing compile pass must have PCRE2_AUTO_CALLOUT set in this option word.

Source. The current pattern item is the lone '&', so parse_regex does not treat it as a quantifier. That accepted branch consumes the attacker-controlled byte and routes this item through manage_callouts(), which is the path that can synthesize an automatic callout ahead of it.

With PCRE2_AUTO_CALLOUT set, manage_callouts allocates a four-word metadata record in parsed_pattern, tags it as META_CALLOUT_NUMBER, and records the current item's pattern offset 0. This materializes the accepted '&' item as callout state.

compile_regex lowers the synthetic META_CALLOUT_NUMBER record into an executable OP_CALLOUT item in the compiled pattern. The runtime matching loop therefore dispatches do_callout() before processing the literal '&'.

After compilation succeeds, the harness requests callout support for later matching by passing callout_function and &callout_count into pcre2_set_callout(). Without this request, do_callout would later return immediately on a NULL callback.

pcre2_set_callout stores the non-NULL callback pointer and counter address into the match context. This is the source-level callback state that later has to be transferred into the active match block.
Before the main matching loop runs, match() copies the callback state from mcontext into mb. This is the missing causal link between pcre2_set_callout() and do_callout's later mb->callout check.

When the injected OP_CALLOUT item executes, do_callout checks the copied match-block field. Because step 7 populated mb->callout from the registered callback, this guard is false and execution continues into the compatibility offset_vector setup.

Sink and root cause. Fovector is the macro alias for `F->ovector`, and `heapframe` declares `PCRE2_SIZE ovector[2]` as its final field. This statement forms a pointer two elements before that declared array to mimic the legacy extended ovector layout; the next vulnerable lines then save and restore `Fovector[-2]` and `Fovector[-1]` as those synthetic slots. UBSan reports the backwards step at this exact line as 'index -2 out of bounds for type size_t [2]'.

Crash site. do_callout subtracts two elements from Fovector and stores the resulting backwards pointer relative to the declared two-element array in cb.offset_vector.
The compatibility pointer value established for the legacy two-slot view is the same pointer value stored into `cb.offset_vector` at the sink.
